title: Is every timestamp with a tooltip a Tab stop?
context: The spec as it reads today (2026-10-24) already says this; the question was written against an older wording. The sentence is unclear. The code settles it: a timestamp is a Tab stop exactly when its tooltip is on. The tooltip is on by default for relative times and date labels, and can be turned on for any format.

current.text: A timestamp with its tooltip is a Tab stop, so keyboard users can reach the full date and time; the tooltip is on by default for relative times and date labels.
With the tooltip it is a Tab stop; focus shows the full moment.
With the tooltip the <time> is a Tab stop, so keyboard users can reach the full value; the tooltip describes it.

renders.caption: Tab through: the first two are stops, the third is not
renders.jsx: h(P.Stack, { gap: 'sm' }, h(P.Time, { value: Date.now() - 300000, format: 'relative' }), h(P.Time, { value: Date.now() - 86400000, format: 'datetime', tooltip: true }), h(P.Time, { value: Date.now() - 86400000, format: 'datetime' }))

options.label: Tab stop when the tooltip is on
options.text: Wording: "A timestamp with its tooltip is a Tab stop, so keyboard users can reach the full date. The tooltip is on by default for relative times and date labels."

render.caption: Tooltip on, any format
render.jsx: h(P.Time, { value: Date.now() - 86400000, format: 'date', tooltip: true })

options.label: Only relative times and labels
options.text: Wording ties focus to the format; a datetime with tooltip on would not be reachable, so the code would change.

render.caption: Relative only
render.jsx: h(P.Time, { value: Date.now() - 300000, format: 'relative' })

recommendation: A: a Tab stop whenever the tooltip is on. That is what the code does, and WCAG 1.4.13 and the APG tooltip pattern require tooltip content to be reachable by keyboard focus.
